linux.fallback: configured shares as written, not live nfsd/smbd state; Samba registry backend, include= files and usershares are not read (constrained token); a symlinked config file or exports.d is refused
linux.mechanism: bounded no-follow reads of /etc/exports, /etc/exports.d/*.exports and /etc/samba/smb.conf (pure parsers); one lstat of the usershares directory

macos.fallback: SMB share points from sharing(8) and NFS exports as configured in /etc/exports; the sharepoints dslocal node is not read
macos.mechanism: subprocess_runner:/usr/sbin/sharing -l -f json plus a bounded no-follow read of /etc/exports (BSD syntax)

windows.fallback: not read yet: one unsupported status row, windows:planned

caveats: **No documented customer driver.** No documented customer driver for this plugin was found (as in `mgmt_posture`'s caveat); it exists to answer what this host exposes over SMB and NFS, which no other plugin reports. Pure capability-gap reasoning.

**Configured, not live; some Samba scope is not read.** Linux reports what the files say, not whether `nfsd` or `smbd` runs or what a client sees. The Samba registry backend, `include =` files and usershares (including a Debian build's compiled-in usershare default, which the file does not show: the directory `lstat` is the detection) are reported as `constrained` tokens, never as a wrong share list. A symlinked `/etc/exports`, `smb.conf` or `/etc/exports.d` (a NixOS-style `/etc`) is refused rather than followed, and a containerised agent reads the image's `/etc`, not the host's.

**Windows is planned.** The `NetShareEnum` level-2 read, which will flag the administrative `STYPE_SPECIAL` shares (`ADMIN$`, `IPC$`, drive shares) as `special` rather than hide them, is not implemented; the leg reports one `unsupported` row, `windows:planned`.

**macOS scope and an unverified edge.** macOS reports SMB share points from `sharing -l -f json` and NFS from `/etc/exports`; the `sharepoints` directory-service node is not read (permission denied unprivileged). The output of `sharing` with no share points at all has not been observed (the reference Mac has one), so whitespace or `{}` is read as an empty list and any other text reports `unrecognised_output`; the `/etc/exports` parser follows `man exports` but has only been exercised on reconstructed fixtures, because the reference Mac has no such file.
**Names and paths can identify people.** See the sensitivity bullet: a share name or path may contain an account name, so the plugin is gated at `Infrastructure:Read` and the definition says so.

definitions.description: Reports the shares this host is configured to serve over SMB and NFS: name, path, ro/rw/mixed, whether anonymous access is allowed and a few flags, never ACLs or NFS client host lists (clients are a count). On Linux, read from /etc/exports, /etc/exports.d and /etc/samba/smb.conf as written, not live nfsd/smbd state; the Samba registry backend, include files and usershares are not read. On macOS, SMB share points from the sharing tool plus /etc/exports. The Windows leg is planned and not yet read. A refused or failed read is permission_denied or constrained with a reason token, never an empty result; one source row per source says whether it was read. Share names and paths can embed account names, so the result is sensitive. A leading status row states whether the read was complete.

description: Shares this host serves over SMB/NFS: names, paths and a few flags, never ACLs
how_it_works:
`list` reports the shares this host is configured to serve over SMB and NFS: names, paths, read-only or read-write, whether anonymous access is allowed, and a few flags. It reads local configuration (Linux) or asks one built-in tool and reads one file (macOS) and changes nothing. The first row is always a `status` row saying whether the read was complete, then one `source` row per source the leg knows about (so zero `share` rows is never an ambiguous empty success), then the `share` rows. These are configured exports, not live `nfsd` or `smbd` state, and they are not the mapped-drive and session observations `tar` records for `mapdrive` (which track mappings this host makes and sessions against its shares). ACLs, `valid users` and NFS client host lists are never emitted: an NFS export carries a client count (`clients_<n>`) and an `anonymous` flag only.

On Linux the leg reads `/etc/exports`, the `/etc/exports.d/*.exports` snippets and `/etc/samba/smb.conf` with bounded reads that never follow a symlink, under one row and byte budget per listing. The exports files use the `exports(5)` grammar. `smb.conf` is parsed with Samba's own semantics: parameter synonyms collapse to one key so the last occurrence wins, a `copy =` chain and `[global]` are consulted when a share does not set a value itself, and Samba's built-in defaults apply last. On macOS the leg runs `/usr/sbin/sharing -l -f json` through the bounded runner for SMB share points and reads `/etc/exports` (the BSD `exports(5)` grammar that macOS `nfsd` reads) for NFS.
name: shares

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (field 0). Values: status, source, share.
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: status: the literal "list". source: exports, exports_d, smb_conf or sharing. share: nfs or smb.
columns.name: field_1

columns.description: status: supported, constrained, permission_denied or unsupported (Windows and a leg that threw). source: read, absent, refused or failed (absent is a state, not a failure). share: the SMB share name, or "-" for NFS (identified by path).
columns.name: field_2

columns.description: status: reason token(s) for a non-supported read, "-" when complete; tokens look like linux:shares:exports:permission_denied, linux:shares:smb_conf:registry_backend, macos:shares:sharing:exit_nonzero, subprocess_runner:deadline, windows:planned. source: the number of shares read from it, "-" unless it was read. share: the exported path ("-" when none is set).
columns.name: field_3

columns.description: share: ro, rw, mixed (clients or security flavours disagree) or "-" when unknown. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_4

columns.description: share: true when anonymous (guest or world) access is allowed, false when not, "-" when unknown. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_5

columns.description: share: comma-separated flags from hidden, unavailable, special, sealed, no_root_squash, clients_<n> (the NFS client count; hosts are never listed), or "-". Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_6

columns.description: share: the source it came from (exports, exports_d, smb_conf or sharing). Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_7

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited; field 0 is the row kind, `-` is an absent value, and the first row is always `status|list|<supported\|constrained\|permission_denied\|unsupported>|<reason or ->`. A `source|<exports\|exports_d\|smb_conf\|sharing>|<read\|absent\|refused\|failed>|<share count or ->` row follows for every source the leg knows about (Linux three, macOS two: `exports` and `sharing`; `absent` is a state, not a failure). Each share is `share|<nfs\|smb>|<name or ->|<path or ->|<ro\|rw\|mixed\|->|<true\|false\|->|<flags or ->|<source>`: the name is the SMB share name and `-` for NFS (identified by path), `mixed` means clients or security flavours disagree, and the flags are a closed set: `hidden`, `unavailable`, `special` (Samba `[homes]`, `[printers]`, `[print$]`), `sealed`, `no_root_squash` and `clients_<n>`. Every free field is scrubbed of NUL and invalid UTF-8 and pipe-escaped.

privileges.grant: None for `sharing -l -f json`, which lists share points to an unprivileged caller; `/etc/exports` is read with the agent's own permissions (not measured: the reference Mac has no such file)
privileges.if_refused: `CONSTRAINED` / partial with a `subprocess_runner:*` or `macos:shares:*` token; `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial only when `/etc/exports` was refused and nothing was read; `UNAVAILABLE` / unknown with `subprocess_runner:spawn_error` when the tool could not be started
privileges.measured: `sharing` measured unprivileged (euid 501) on the reference Mac, 2026-10-12; `/etc/exports` is absent on that host, so the read is untested against a real file (caveat 4)

privileges.grant: None: `/etc/exports`, `/etc/exports.d/*.exports` and `/etc/samba/smb.conf` are world-readable (0644) on stock packages. A site that tightens them can grant read access to the agent account, or accept the token
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `linux:shares:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read; the source row says `refused`
privileges.measured: Not measured on the `yuzu` account; see Sample output for the capture
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu`), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every source that exists was read in full; no shares is `supported` with `absent` or `read|0` source rows

Linux: a source could not be read (a symlinked file or `exports.d`, a FIFO, a file over 256 KiB, a NUL byte, an unreadable directory, more than 64 snippets or 4096 directory entries); its source row says `failed` and the other sources are still reported

Linux: the Samba shares are incomplete by design: a registry backend (`config backend = registry`, `registry shares = yes`), a live `include =`, a `copy =` target that is missing, cyclic or deeper than 8, or usershares (configured, or the usershares directory exists)
more than 512 shares or 1 MiB of share text across all sources (the listing stops there), or a name or path over 4096 bytes was cut

macOS: `sharing` exited nonzero, its output was truncated or was not a JSON object, a record had no string `path` (the valid ones are still emitted), or `/etc/exports` could not be read (same causes as Linux)

macOS: `sharing` ran but timed out, was cancelled, was killed by a signal or hit the 8192-line cap, or (`spawn_error`) `/usr/sbin/sharing` could not be started; `/etc/exports` is still read; `source|sharing|failed`
a source was refused and no source was read; accumulated constrained tokens may follow, comma-joined
a leg threw: an `unsupported` status row, reported instead of unwinding across the plugin boundary

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. `list` is also a gathered definition (`crossplatform.network.shares`, 3600s TTL).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync, TAR, DEX, or metrics.

**Sensitivity.** Share names and paths can embed account names: Samba `[homes]` and per-user shares, macOS record names such as "<Name>'s Public Folder" and `/Users/<name>/Public`. Treat the result as sensitive; it is gated at `Infrastructure:Read`. No ACLs, `valid users` lists or NFS client host lists are read into a row; NFS clients are a count and an anonymous flag.
**Siblings:** `tar` `mapdrive` (the mapped drives and sessions this host makes and receives, not the exports it offers) and `network_config`.
